metadata.title: Stop at the First Match with break
metadata.description: Find the first name that starts with S and stop searching immediately using break.

instructions.main: Given `names = ["Anna", "Sam", "Grace", "Simon", "Tina"]`, find the FIRST name that starts with `S` and stop searching as soon as you find it. Store it in `first`.
steps: When you find a match, store it in `first` and `break` out of the loop.

hints.message: Start with `for name in names:` and test `name.startswith("S")` inside the loop.
The task wants the FIRST match only — use `break` to leave the loop as soon as you find it.
Iterate with a `for name in names:` loop — a `while` loop plus manual index tracking is not needed here.
Inside the `if`, assign `first = name` and then call `break` on the next line.

evaluation.feedback_on_all_pass: Your loop finds the first S-name and stops immediately.

test_cases.feedback_on_pass: You use break in a loop that is not a while loop.
test_cases.feedback_on_fail: Use a `for` loop over `names` and `break` out of it right after you find the first match.
